🎙
Opening remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with Chairman of the Transitional Sovereignty Council of the Republic of the Sudan Abdel Fattah al-Burhan on the sidelines of
the Third Russia–Africa Summit
(Moscow, October 30, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
First of all, thank you once again for finding the time to visit us and participate in
the Russia–Africa Summit
. Today, we have an opportunity to discuss
our bilateral relations
.
🇷🇺
🇸🇩
I would like to stress that Sudan is an important partner for Russia in the Arab world and on the African continent.
Earlier this year, in January, if I recall correctly, we marked
the 70th anniversary
of the establishment of diplomatic relations
.
Our bilateral cooperation is friendly and constructive.
Despite the difficulties Sudan has faced, our relations continue to develop, including in trade and economic affairs.
📈
Russia-Sudan trade more than doubled in 2025 and grew by a further 25% in January-August 2026
– a very positive trend. Sudan ranks among Russia’s ten leading trading partners in Africa.
Our bilateral intergovernmental commission is active and held a meeting in Moscow last September.
Russian educational institutions are training Sudanese professionals.
This year, 1
00 state-funded places
were allocated to Sudanese citizens. Next year, the quota will increase to
140
.
We are, of course, closely following the situation in Sudan
, where the armed conflict has continued for more than three years. We understand the difficult circumstances facing the Sudanese people. According to our information, the number of refugees and internally displaced persons has
exceeded 13 million
. The economy and infrastructure have suffered damage.
Russia has contributed to humanitarian assistance
, including through
the UN World Food Programme
.
Russia has consistently advocated an end to hostilities and a political settlement.
As we agreed, we can discuss these sensitive issues further in private and exchange views on what else Russia could do to help normalise the situation in Sudan, as well as on other pressing matters.
As for prospects for
cooperation in trade, the economy, industry and high technology
, you and, I expect, your colleagues have seen
what Russia has to offer
in modern areas of cooperation, particularly
digital technology, healthcare, education and logistics
.
🤝
We have prepared a roadmap covering these areas, which we consider promising
. I would like to give it to you and ask you to instruct your aides and members of the Sudanese Government to examine it carefully and identify the areas you consider most interesting and suitable for joint work.
#RussiaSudan

🎙
Opening remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with President of Kenya William Samoei Ruto on the sidelines of
the Third Russia–Africa Summit
(Moscow, October 29, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
Diplomatic relations between our countries were established back in 1963, and we are gradually approaching
their 65th anniversary
.
We maintain
regular political dialogue
at various levels
. I remember your predecessor attending
the first Summit in Sochi in 2019
. Kenya has participated in all three summits. Our foreign ministers
exchange visits
, and our parliaments maintain
regular contacts
.
🇷🇺
🇰🇪
We are interested in further developing trade and economic cooperation with Kenya.
I would like to note that
bilateral trade almost doubled
in January-August of this year. This is a positive trend that we must sustain.
Supplies of Russian agricultural products have increased
. Russia is also one of the leading exporters of fertilisers. Once again, I would like to stress the importance of maintaining this positive momentum.
We maintain fruitful cultural and humanitarian ties.
We help train Kenyan professionals and are gradually increasing the scholarship quota for your young people, who, as I understand it, enjoy studying in Russia.
70 scholarships
have been allocated for civilian fields of study next year.
Russian performing arts groups regularly visit Kenya.
The Russian Ballet Academic Theatre
performed there last December, followed by
the Khokhloma ensemble
in June and
the Rossiya ensemble
in September, among others. Just a month ago, Nairobi hosted
a Day of Russian Culture
. Kenyan performers also participate in international music competitions in Russia.
🤝
We share positions on a number of key international issues
, including strengthening the UN’s central role, the importance of respecting
its Charter
, and building a
#MultipolarWorld
order.
Nairobi hosts a UN office
, and we support further strengthening Kenya’s role in this universal organisation.
It is the only UN headquarters located in a country of the Global South. Nairobi has even earned the unofficial title of the world’s environmental capital. We are very pleased about this, and much of it is thanks to the efforts of the Kenyan people themselves.
Russia consistently advocated establishing a UN office in Kenya
. We support strengthening it, stepping up negotiations, and locating the secretariats of new environmental mechanisms and agreements there.
#RussiaKenya

item.title: ⚡️ Russia’s Minister of Sport Mikhail Degtyarev The Court of Arbitration for Sport #CAS
item.description: ⚡️ Russia’s Minister of Sport Mikhail Degtyarev : The Court of Arbitration for Sport ( #CAS ) has ordered the International Ice Hockey Federation ( #IIHF ) to admit Russian national teams to international competitions . CAS overturned all five resolutions adopted by the IIHF Council and ordered that Russian teams be allowed to compete in the IIHF events covered by those resolutions. CAS thus upheld the key claims of the Ice Hockey Federation of Russia and overturned the IIHF decisions that prevented Russian teams from participating in international competitions. ❗️ Under the ruling , the IIHF must ensure Russian teams’ participation in the relevant tournaments in the 2026/27 season. The CAS ruling settles this issue, as it is final and cannot be appealed . Challenging work lies ahead as we work with the IIHF to implement the CAS ruling and secure Russian teams’ return to competitions held under its auspices. 🏒 The next event is the World Junior Championship , which will take place in the Canadian cities of Edmonton and Red Deer.

item.title: 🎙 Opening remarks by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with Chairperson of the African Union, President of Burundi Evariste Ndayishimiye on the sidelines of
item.description: 🎙 Opening remarks by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with Chairperson of the African Union, President of Burundi Evariste Ndayishimiye on the sidelines of the Third Russia–Africa Summit (Moscow, October 29, 2026) 💬 Vladimir Putin: I would like to thank you for your substantial contribution to the success of our Summit . We are developing relations with the African Union , which you currently chair, on a solid, long-term basis . As you know, we supported your aspiration to become a full member of the #G20 . 🇷🇺 🇧🇮 Our bilateral relations are progressing well, and our ties continue to grow. We can discuss what further steps we can take to ensure that both political and economic cooperation underpin our shared plans for developing bilateral ties. These ties go back many years. Next year, we will mark the 65th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. 🎓 Mr President, I understand that yesterday you were awarded an honorary doctorate from Patrice Lumumba Peoples’ Friendship University of Russia ( #RUDN ). Please accept my warmest congratulations on this occasion. #RussiaBurundi

🎙
Opening remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with President of the Republic of the Congo Denis Sassou Nguesso on the sidelines of
the Third Russia–Africa Summit
(Moscow, October 29, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
We worked together at both
the First
and
Second Russia–Africa Summits
, held in Sochi and St Petersburg. Today, together with our other African friends, we have completed
the Third Summit
.
In my view,
the outcome
is very satisfactory indeed.
We have achieved virtually all the objectives we set ourselves.
🇷🇺
🇨🇬
Our bilateral relations are developing successfully.
We maintain
regular political dialogue
, expand trade and economic ties, and strengthen scientific, technical and humanitarian cooperation.
Last year, we concluded
an important intergovernmental agreement on the promotion and reciprocal protection of investments
. Russia
has already completed the domestic procedures
required for its entry into force.
The eighth meeting of the intergovernmental commission
took place
in Brazzaville on September 28-30
. As we agreed, a plan for the comprehensive development of cooperation between the Russian Federation and the Republic of the Congo for 2026-2028 has been signed.
Currently,
863 students from the Republic of the Congo are studying at Russian educational institutions
. This cooperation rests on a solid historical foundation.
Cultural ties are also growing stronger
. In mid-July, Brazzaville hosted
a three-day festival of Russian language and culture
entitled
“We Are Together”
, which concluded with an open day dedicated to Russian education.
🤝
Mr President, we will certainly
continue to move forward
at the same pace in all these areas.
#RussiaCongo
